question: In the Board UI improvements epic, the recovery design gives every seat two positions in its feed rather than one. Why two, and what may never advance them?
expected: Because a seat can crash between delivery and action: one position is the transport cursor (what was delivered) and the other is a processed watermark (what the seat actually acted on), and the resume delta is computed from the processed watermark so unresolved asks replay. Neither watermark may be advanced by a bare inbox() or record_status call - an ask stays open until the seat answers that exact message id (reply_to) or the sender resolves it.

question: In the redesigned board interface, if someone types formatting marks or a snippet of page code into a message, what does the reader see, and what does become clickable?
expected: Exactly the characters typed: message text is rendered as plain text, with no Markdown and no HTML, so nothing can be styled or injected through a message. A deliberately narrow pass over the text turns only two things into links - @handles that resolve to a participant, and artifact ids that resolve to a real artifact.

question: In the Space Travel project, how are the pictures used as measurement evidence actually taken from the engine, and which routes were abandoned?
expected: By running the packaged game (-game -unattended -windowed with the map on the command line) under a dedicated game mode that requests an in-game screenshot per pose into Saved/, with a manifest, and measuring the decoded PNGs afterwards. The editor-side capture paths were dropped because they render the editor's level rather than the runtime scene, and the offscreen SceneCapture2D attempt in the automation commandlet was ruled a dead end and abandoned by order.
